content.thinking:
I need to use figure labels as references rather than my own numbers, tracing the causal chain starting from the symptom: shoppers seeing stale spend totals because cached figures disagreed, citing the relevant alert evidence, then digging into why the cache stopped updating.

Looking at the read path, it served entries without reconciling items counted against actual purchases, which is unverified from the static evidence. But as for why the updates actually stopped in the first place, the available records don't show a triggering change—no production deploys, no flag flips, no clear placement shift—so the chain seems to run out at that point, with limited log and metric evidence to go further.

Given that, I'd mark reaches_a_cause as false, since the root cause of the stoppage remains unknown and the read-path behavior itself is unverified. Contributing factors include the lack of validation on the read side and a detection gap—no alert fired on the update path stalling, only after stale copies started being served. I'm thinking the remaining action items should cover investigating why updates stopped, adding an alert for cache update lag, and restoring log/metric observability, numbered as the next set after the existing ones.

For the executive summary, I want to avoid specific identifiers like PR numbers or pod names and instead use the generic placeholders for duration and figures affected, noting that purchases themselves were never impacted and the stale totals were caught and reverted to the ledger. I should flag that the root cause is still unknown and could recur, while crediting the quick mitigation and intact ledger data as things that went well, with the empty metrics/logs as a clear gap.

I'm now working out the timing details—gap between when copies went stale versus when they were served, plus the detection lag between that and the alert firing—while noting key assumptions like the unverified fix and uncertain error rate before writing the final version.

action_items.item: Find out why cache updates stopped when purchases were recorded from {A5}, by examining the process that writes or invalidates the cached spend totals outside this repository, and restore it. Then confirm that new purchases update the cached figures.

Add an alert on the cached spend totals falling behind recorded purchases, firing when the update path stops. It should fire before stale figures are served, not only when reconciliation finds a mismatch.
Make the incident metrics and service logs for this service readable during an investigation, and alert when a query returns nothing for a service that should be reporting.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers were shown cached spend totals that disagreed with their purchases. {A1} of {A2} figures were behind, by at most {A4} purchase each and by a widest gap of {A3}. The figures were being served from {A6}. The impact figures are lower bounds, and the error rate could not be read.

The cached copies were behind because they stopped keeping up with newly recorded purchases from {A5}, while the purchase records stayed correct. Discarding the {T22.2} stale entries was confirmed, with nothing to put back, which shows the copies were derived data and the ledger was right.

The stale copies reached shoppers because the account page served any cached entry it got back without comparing its stored purchase count with the purchases already loaded. Nothing noticed until the reconciliation check raised the alert. This comes from a static reading of the source that nothing ran, so it is unverified.

The cached copies stopped being updated for a reason the evidence does not show. Nothing in the repository writes to or invalidates the cache, so that part sits outside the code read. The record rules out some triggers: no production changes were read back in either window searched, and the flag provider showed no recent flag changes. Metrics and service logs came back empty, so nothing shows what happened to the update path. The chain stops here.

contributing_factors.factor: The page read path was not seen to check a cached entry against the purchases it already had, so a stalled update path put stale figures in front of shoppers. The proposed fix is open and unmerged.

No check was seen that watches whether cache updates are keeping up. The copies fell behind from {A5}, were served from {A6}, and the alert came only at {alert_raised}, which is {alert_raised - A6} after serving began. Detection came from a later reconciliation check, not from the update path.
The mitigation discarded stale entries once, but nothing was seen restoring the update path, so figures go stale again as shoppers buy and a later check will name more.
The incident metrics and service logs could not be read, so the investigation had no data on why the updates stopped. Metrics returned {T5.2} minutes and logs returned {T11.2} lines.

input.executive_summary: Some shoppers' account pages showed out-of-date spend totals. {A1} of {A2} cached figures were behind the purchase records, each missing at most {A4} purchase. The purchase records themselves were correct, so no purchase data was lost. The out-of-date figures were being shown from {A6}, and the service was affected for at least {duration}, which is a lower bound. Argus discarded the stale cached figures, so those pages go back to the purchase records, and it marked the incident mitigated. The record does not show why the cached figures stopped being updated, and nothing has been seen to correct that. Figures can therefore go stale again as shoppers keep buying. A draft code change is open for review.

got_lucky: The purchase ledger stayed correct, so discarding the cache was safe and no purchase data was affected.
Each stale figure was missing at most {A4} purchase, so the errors were small.
went_well: Argus mitigated by discarding the stale figures, and the store reported removing what was wrong. Pages fall back to the purchase ledger, which never moved.
A draft fix was proposed that serves a cached entry only when it matches the purchases, and reports a mismatch in the logs.
The alert named the affected figures and the gap in them, which made the scope clear.
went_wrong: The cause of the updates stopping was not found. The metrics and log reads came back empty, and no production or flag change was seen to explain it.
The mitigation clears the symptom only. Nothing is putting the copies right, so more figures can go stale.
Detection came from a reconciliation check rather than from the update path itself.

input.root_cause: The cached spend totals stopped being updated when purchases were recorded, from {A5}. The evidence does not show why the update or invalidation path stopped. The account page then served whatever cached entry it found without checking it against the purchases it already had loaded. That is a static reading of the code (F1) that nothing ran, so it is unverified.
input.symptom: Account pages showed out-of-date spend totals
